exact_text:
(1) These rules may be called the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020.
(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.
legal_status_notes: Published in Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II, Sec 3(i) vide G.S.R. 462(E) on 23 July 2020.

exact_text:
(1) Save as otherwise expressly provided by the Central Government by notification, these rules shall apply to—
(a) all goods and services bought or sold over digital or electronic network including digital products;
(b) all models of e-commerce, including marketplace and inventory models of e-commerce;
(c) all e-commerce retail, including multi-channel single brand retailers and single brand retailers in single or multiple formats; and
(d) all forms of unfair trade practices across all models of e-commerce:
Provided that these rules shall not apply to any activity of a natural person carried out in a personal capacity not being part of any professional or commercial activity undertaken on a regular or systematic basis.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (1), these rules shall apply to an e-commerce entity which is not established in India, but systematically offers goods or services to consumers in India.
legal_status_notes: Applies extra-territorially to overseas e-commerce entities offering goods/services to consumers in India.
Defines core operational entities in digital commerce.
Enforced vide G.S.R. 462(E). Mandates 48-hour acknowledgment, 1-month resolution, ban on pre-ticked boxes, refund compliance.
Enforced vide G.S.R. 462(E). Imposes mandatory disclosures and ranking transparency on platforms.
Enforced vide G.S.R. 462(E). Prohibits fake reviews and mandates refund for defective/late goods.

section_or_rule_title: Duties and liabilities of inventory e-commerce entities
exact_text:
(1) Every inventory e-commerce entity which dishes out direct sales to consumers shall provide in a clear and accessible manner displayed prominently on its platform:—
(a) accurate information relating to return, refund, exchange, warranty and guarantee, delivery and shipment, cost of return shipping, modes of payment, security of payment methods, and grievance redressal mechanism;
(b) total price in single figure along with the breakup price for the good or service, showing all the compulsory and optional charges, and the applicable tax code;
(c) all mandatory notices and information provided by applicable law, and the country of origin of the goods and services offered for sale.
(2) No inventory e-commerce entity shall falsely represent itself as a consumer and post reviews about goods and services or misrepresent the quality or the features of any goods or services.
(3) Every inventory e-commerce entity shall ensure that the advertisements for marketing of goods or services are consistent with the actual characteristics, access and usage conditions of such goods or services.
(4) No inventory e-commerce entity shall refuse to take back goods, or withdraw or discontinue services purchased or agreed to be purchased, or refuse to refund consideration paid for goods or services, if such goods or services are defective, deficient, spurious, or if the goods or services are not of the characteristics or features as advertised or as agreed to, or if such goods or services are delivered late from the stated delivery schedule: Provided that in the case of late delivery, this sub-rule shall not apply if such late delivery was due to force majeure.
(5) Every inventory e-commerce entity shall explicitly specify the expiry date of the goods offered for sale to consumers on its platform.
legal_status_notes: Enforced vide G.S.R. 462(E). Holds inventory models strictly liable for defects, false reviews, and refunds.

exact_text: The provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019) shall apply for any contravention of the provisions of these rules.
legal_status_notes: Enforced vide G.S.R. 462(E). Directs penalties under CPA 2019.
